title: Attribution + UTM Conventions (Lifecycle Growth Sprint)
content:
Owner: Tyler Benson (Marketing Ops)
Last updated: 2025-01-22
Scope: PLG lifecycle growth sprint (onboarding emails + in-console nudges + retargeting). This doc defines UTM standards, campaign naming rules, and how we join marketing touches to product activation/retention events.

---

1) Goals / why this exists
- Make attribution consistent across Email + Paid (LinkedIn/Google) + “in-product-to-docs” clicks.
- Enable reliable slicing of activation funnel metrics by campaign/audience/creative in the activation dashboards.
- Avoid “UTM spaghetti” (random strings, inconsistent casing) and prevent privacy/compliance surprises.

Non-goals
- This is not a full MMM/MTA system. We’re doing practical “good enough” attribution for sprint decisions.
- Not defining Sales-assisted attribution (HubSpot lifecycle stage influence). That’s separate.

---

2) Required UTM parameters (and strict formatting)
We will standardize on the canonical 5 UTMs:
- utm_source (REQUIRED)
- utm_medium (REQUIRED)
- utm_campaign (REQUIRED)
- utm_content (RECOMMENDED for creative/variant)
- utm_term (OPTIONAL; only when truly meaningful, e.g., Google search keyword group)

Formatting rules
- Lowercase only
- Use underscores, not spaces or hyphens (exceptions: “rwi” prefix allowed as literal)
- No PII in any UTM value (no email, no full name, no company name, no user id)
- Keep values < 80 chars where possible (some downstream tools truncate)

Allowed characters
- a–z, 0–9, underscore

Examples (good)
- utm_source=google
- utm_medium=paid_search
- utm_campaign=rwi_lifecycle_activation_retgt_nonactivated_wk1_20250115
- utm_content=benchmarks_v1_static_300x250

Examples (bad)
- utm_campaign=Activation Sprint - Week 1 (spaces/case)
- utm_content=soojin-review-final!! (punctuation)
- utm_term=jane_doe@company.com (PII)

---

3) Standard vocabulary (source + medium)
We use a small controlled list so reporting isn’t a mess.

utm_source (choose one)
- email (if sent via lifecycle tooling; see note below)
- google
- linkedin
- x
- reddit
- organic (only if we intentionally tag organic posts; otherwise leave untagged)
- partner (rare; requires explicit partner name in utm_campaign, not in source)

utm_medium (choose one)
- lifecycle_email
- paid_search
- paid_social
- display
- sponsored_post
- referral

Note on email “source”
- We keep utm_source=email for all lifecycle email sends.
- Vendor/platform is NOT a source. If we need vendor diagnostics, use a non-UTM param (e.g., rwi_mailer=customerio) but do not rely on it for reporting.

---

4) Campaign naming convention (utm_campaign)
utm_campaign is the key we’ll join on in dashboards. It must encode what we need to answer: “which initiative, which audience, which timeframe.”

Schema
rwi_<initiative>_<goal>_<channel_or_motion>_<audience>_<timebox>_<yyyymmdd>

Definitions
- initiative: lifecycle | docs | launch | webinar | etc.
- goal: activation | retention | reactivation | billing
- channel_or_motion: welcome | onboarding | retgt | newsletter | etc.
- audience: nonactivated | lapsed_d14 | all_signups | sdk_ts | sdk_py | enterprise_eval (keep to a compact controlled list)
- timebox: wk1 | wk2 | always_on
- yyyymmdd: date campaign is first active (start date)

Examples
- rwi_lifecycle_activation_onboarding_nonactivated_wk1_20250115
- rwi_lifecycle_reactivation_retgt_lapsed_d14_wk2_20250122
- rwi_lifecycle_activation_welcome_all_signups_always_on_20250115

If the campaign must roll forward (same concept, new creative):
- Keep utm_campaign the same for the “initiative rollup”
- Differentiate creative via utm_content (see below)

---

5) Creative/variant naming (utm_content)
utm_content should capture creative + variant. Keep it deterministic.

Schema
<message_theme>_<format>_<variant>

Examples
- quickstart_static_v1
- benchmarks_video_v2
- troubleshooting_text_v1

If A/B testing subject lines (email):
- Use utm_content=subject_a vs subject_b (or include theme: welcome_subject_a)

If A/B testing landing page variants:
- Use utm_content=lp_quickstart_v1 vs lp_quickstart_v2
- Also pass rwi_lp=quickstart_variant (non-UTM param) if the web team wants it, but UTM content is the reporting key.

---

6) Landing page + console link rules
Where possible, all campaign clicks should land on:
- a stable docs page, OR
- a stable marketing landing page, OR
- a stable console route.

Rules
- Do not deep-link into console routes that are not stable (we already hit 404 risk with routing changes).
- Prefer “/console/quickstart” style routes that are maintained by Console team.
- Every email CTA must be checked against current routing + feature flags before launch.

Redirect policy
- If we use short links / redirects, redirects must preserve query params (UTMs) end-to-end.
- Redirect must be 302/307 (not dropping query strings).

---

7) What we capture in product analytics events (event properties)
We will capture UTMs at the edge and propagate into product events as properties where available.

Canonical properties (stored on events when known)
- utm_source
- utm_medium
- utm_campaign
- utm_content
- utm_term
- referrer
- landing_url
- gclid (Google click id, if present)
- li_fat_id (LinkedIn click id, if present)

Important: we treat click IDs as marketing identifiers; they are not user PII, but still sensitive. Storage/retention must follow the marketing tracking data review.

At minimum, capture UTMs on these milestone events (see event taxonomy):
- signup_completed
- api_key_created
- first_request_success
- first_streaming_success
- dashboard_viewed (latency/cost dashboard)
- billing_added

(Engineering link: ENG-2844 / PR-8944 should ensure UTMs are available server-side and client-side where possible.)

---

8) Joining logic: how we connect campaign touches to product activation
We need a deterministic join path for dashboards.

Entities / identifiers (high level)
- anonymous_id (browser/device scoped; changes across browsers)
- user_id (Redwood account user id after signup/login)
- email_hash (only if approved; do not store raw email in analytics events)

Primary join approach (recommended)
1) On first site visit / landing page hit: store UTMs in a first-party cookie/local storage with timestamp.
2) On signup/login: create an identify/alias mapping from anonymous_id -> user_id.
3) On subsequent product events: attach the “latest known UTMs” for that user (within window) plus “first-touch UTMs” if we support both.

Attribution model for sprint dashboards (explicit)
- Primary: last non-direct click within 7 days prior to milestone event time.
- Secondary (diagnostic): first-touch within 14 days prior to milestone.

Definitions
- “Direct” = no utm_* and referrer is empty or same-site.
- We only attribute to a campaign if utm_campaign is present.

Edge cases / caveats
- Multiple devices: user clicks email on phone, activates on laptop. Attribution may be lost unless login happens on both and we have a cross-device identity stitch.
- Privacy tools/ad blockers: can strip UTMs or block scripts.
- Email clients: can open/click through link scanners; may generate “false” clicks.
- Retargeting: view-through attribution is not used in product dashboards by default (too noisy). Paid platforms will still report view-through; don’t compare apples to apples.

---

9) Dashboard slices we need (minimum viable for sprint readout)
Every activation/retention chart in the sprint readout should be sliceable by:
- utm_campaign
- utm_source
- utm_medium
- utm_content (creative variant)
- geography (region)
- SDK (ts/python/other) where available

If a chart can’t be sliced reliably due to missing UTMs, we must label it “partial attribution” and include the % of events with attribution coverage.

---

10) Operational checklist (before launch)
Email (Lifecycle)
- [ ] All CTA links have UTMs appended and validated (no broken routing / no 404)
- [ ] Suppression/unsubscribe links are NOT tagged with UTMs
- [ ] Test click through -> console -> first_request_success includes UTMs on event payload (spot check)

Paid (LinkedIn/Google)
- [ ] Final URLs use canonical UTM schema
- [ ] Ensure auto-tagging doesn’t conflict (Google gclid is OK; keep UTMs anyway)
- [ ] Confirm “campaign name” in ad platform matches utm_campaign (or has a documented mapping)

Landing pages
- [ ] Redirects preserve UTMs
- [ ] Cookies set correctly and expiration matches attribution window

---

11) Mapping table (quick reference)
Channel | utm_source | utm_medium | Notes
Email onboarding series | email | lifecycle_email | One utm_campaign per series timebox; utm_content per email or subject variant
LinkedIn retargeting | linkedin | paid_social | Use utm_content for creative size/type; li_fat_id expected sometimes
Google search | google | paid_search | utm_term optional; gclid may appear
Google display | google | display | treat as separate medium from paid_search

---

12) Open questions / TODOs
- Do we want to store both first-touch and last-touch UTMs on user profile, or only on events? (Product analytics preference?)
- Confirm retention policy for click IDs (gclid, li_fat_id) in our analytics warehouse (see tracking data review).
- Decide whether we want a dedicated “rwi_experiment_id” query param for experiments, separate from utm_campaign, to avoid renaming when experiments iterate.

Change log
- 2025-01-22: Added explicit attribution window + clarified “direct” definition; added controlled vocab for medium.
- 2025-01-15: Initial draft for sprint kickoff.
